final_benchmark_workload.note: np.random.zipf(a=1.3) clipped to 10k ranks, queries 'query_item_N' (NOT in the dataset), 20 seeds

interpretation: A single key ('iphone 16' = rank 1) receives roughly a quarter to a third of all requests under this synthetic Zipf(1.3); whichever node owns that key gets that share on top of ~1/3 of the rest. That is a property of the workload, not of the hash ring, and the 10 000 distinct synthetic keys cap the miss count regardless of cache design.
final_benchmark_concurrency: requests are sent in chunks of 100 with asyncio.gather and the next chunk starts only when the whole chunk finished (closed loop); in-flight requests never exceed 100, not 100 000, and latency excludes queueing that open-loop arrivals would incur
